newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks end weaker on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks end weaker on profit-taking.

text.p: The Singapore stock market ended weaker on profit-taking on Wednesday, dealers said.
They said the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index fell 17.05 points to end at 2,192.45 after unfounded rumours rattled markets in Tokyo and Hong Kong after midday.
"The market is nervous and people just took profits," one dealer said.

Dealers said the tumble was triggered by a fall in the S&P 500 futures traded on GLOBEX in Tokyo. One of the supposed cause for the drop was a newspaper report that Japan investors may cut their purchases of U.S. Treasury debt securities.
Electronic company Uraco topped the actives with 16.7 million shares, including 11.85 million shares crossed at Singapore $0.88 (US$0.63) and S$0.90. The share ended up S$0.015 at S$0.90.

Foreign tranches of Singapore Press Holding and OUB led gainers, rising S$0.40 and S$0.30 respectively to S$26.90 and S$10.80. City Development rose S$0.30 to S$13.10 on 4.2 million shares, including a 3.14 million units crossed at S$12.83-13.00.
Market turnover was 138.7 million shares with losers outpacing gainers by 278 to 92.
Singapore Land led losers, shedding S$0.35 to S$7.65 on 289,000 shares.
